correctness.title: Correctness and regressions
correctness.focus: Behavioral errors, regressions against existing callers, races, cancellation paths, error handling, resource cleanup, and mismatches between the stated task and the implementation.

architecture.title: Ownership and architecture boundaries
architecture.focus: Shared behavior duplicated in CLI and ACP instead of the shared core, provider wire behavior leaking outside box_agent/llm/, tool semantics outside box_agent/tools/, imports that violate the layering checked by tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py, and PPT/document logic added to the core loop instead of Skills. Use docs/design/README.md to find the relevant design document.

security.title: Security, permissions and protocol safety
security.focus: Path escape from the workspace, credential or secret exposure (logs, prompts, errors), command injection, permission or grant bypass, unsafe deserialization, and anything that writes non-protocol output to ACP stdout.

cross-platform.title: macOS / Windows / Linux and packaged runtime
cross-platform.focus: Path separators and drive letters, POSIX-only APIs (termios, fcntl, signals) on Windows, case sensitivity, encoding defaults, subprocess quoting, and differences between source runs and the frozen PyInstaller runtime (IS_FROZEN, bundled packages, external sandbox).

proof.title: Proof coverage
proof.focus: Whether the tests and checks in the change actually exercise the changed behavior and its key failure paths, per the minimum-proof table in docs/PR_REVIEW_STANDARD_CN.md. Report missing coverage only where a concrete regression could slip through.

history.title: History and target-branch consistency
history.focus: Whether this change still works once merged with the target branch. List the inputs, formats, callers and shared APIs the new code relies on, then check the target-branch commits and the merge diff in the context pack for changes to them, including in files this PR does not touch, and read the merged versions. Also report changes that revert or conflict with recent base-branch fixes (see the history file), reintroduce a previously fixed bug, or break a documented compatibility contract.
